nodes.label: W-251 — BUILD116's goldens, and two findings recorded not repaired
nodes.rationale: Both findings are work matter under M's 7 September ruling — a fault in one of the author's instruments and a census whose repair is Phase 3's.

nodes.label: Running the gate without the interpreter shim
nodes.rationale: gate.py runs every instrument as python3 NAME.py hard-coded and ten seated members do not parse before 3.12 (PEP 701), so four goldens failed by a SyntaxError traceback. close_rebank.py regenerates by running, so the tracebacks would have been banked as goldens — the one failure mode a re-bank can have that verify and the census both pass afterwards. The guard held, but it held second.

nodes.label: The nine empty sections are a pointer fault
nodes.rationale: M: 'this is because the citations moved but the pointers did not.' The headings are empty in the live volume and in the Ruling 56 original input alike, so nothing was lost in production; chat 95B's 'authoring gap' conclusion is overturned because the material exists under other numbers. Fifty-one citations resolve to an empty heading, eight of them the Register's, and the Register is append-only — so if the section is ever written it must be written to what those entries already say.

nodes.label: A fabricated citation inside the citation-census instrument
nodes.rationale: 'register 2071' was hard-coded with no measurement behind it and 2071 is a Register LINE, not an entry — exactly the defect the instrument was written to census. The repair removes the class rather than correcting the constant: the instrument now measures which entries own the matching lines, asserted by three new selftest rows.
